verdict.reasoning: Patient reports: "I've just had some diarrhea for the last three days" and describes it as "loose and watery stool."
When asked frequency, patient says: "probably like six or seven times a day." and earlier described this as loose, watery stools.

Patient: "some pain in my, like, lower stomach" and later clarifies "in my lower abdomen...just to one side" and that side is the left; also describes: "it feels, um, like a cramp" and "it comes and goes," supporting intermittent crampy left lower abdominal pain consistent with LLQ.
Patient: "I vomited at the start of the symptoms but now um I've stopped vomiting."

Patient: "I haven't had a fever, um, at the moment, but I did notice um a temperature when the symptoms started, so, um, yeah around about three or four days ago." This supports feeling febrile initially and currently afebrile.
Patient: "yeah i feel a bit uh weak and shaky." and doctor later summarizes "you're quite weak and lethargic."
Patient: "I had a loss of appetite, um, so I haven't been eating as much, but I've been able to hold down fluids." and later describes eating mainly soups/smoothies.
Patient: "I had takeaway about four days ago" and then specifies: "I ate at a Chinese restaurant with friends."
Patient: "so no one else in the family, so a wife and two kids and one, um, child was vomiting, but they haven't got diarrhea." This supports one child with isolated vomiting.
Patient: "other than um athsma, um I use an inhaler, everything else is fine." and to control: Doctor: "And, is your asthma well-controlled?" Patient: "uh, yeah, that's fine... that's under control."
Transcript only states "I use an inhaler" without specifying salbutamol or usage pattern; salbutamol and PRN use are not mentioned.
Occupation: Patient: "I'm an accountant." Household: Doctor: "you live with your wife and two children, is that right?" Patient: "Yes, yeah."
Smoking: Patient: "no, I don't smoke." Alcohol: Patient: "no, I I don't drink alcohol, no."

Doctor: "it seems like you may have something, uh, called gastroenteritis" and explains viral/bacterial causes. Symptoms documented: 3 days of watery diarrhea, left-sided tummy pain (crampy, intermittent), prior vomiting, and patient-reported temperature at onset, aligning with mild fever.
Doctor: "And, is your asthma well-controlled?" Patient: "uh, yeah, that's fine... that's under control." This supports stable asthma.

Doctor: "there are things like Dioralyte you can get from the pharmacy, which... helps replenish your minerals and vitamins" and frames this as part of conservative management for presumed gastroenteritis.

Transcript: "taking some paracetamol, uh, two tablets up to four times a day" (no strength given). The fact specifies 1 g every 6 hours and a 4 g/24 h max, which adds specific dosing not stated and conflicts with the unspecified tablet strength in the transcript.
Doctor: "I will certainly advise you to take some time off work... I would say the next two, two to three days as the infection clears from your system to take some time off and rest."

Doctor: "if your symptoms haven't got better, you know, in in three to four days, I'd like to come and see you again... we may need to do further tests like um taking a sample of your stool so we can test that." This matches return if persistent (3–4 days) and considering stool testing.
The plan section does not mention asthma management or continuing the inhaler; asthma is only discussed in history. No explicit advice to "Continue current inhaler regimen" is given.
